NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
This is the review-only first slice of the three smaller bundles that replace the superseded `C-REVIEW-CURRENT-BOUNDARY-1-217D3F0D`. It completes the review consumer that the first current-only slice (`C-CURRENT-VALIDATION-BOUNDARY-1-D8D7DF85`) left to a dependent bundle, and it removes the last archive-dependent review measurement. The normative source of truth is `spec.xml`; nothing here adds a requirement.
Three findings shape the design. First, the global `MustExist` scan enumerates `changes/**/plan.xml` and parses archived plans before the selected audits run; the authority's call-through read spies show the archive plan read twice through the scan. The global `MustExist` scan must list active plans before reading any plan content, so the removed archive branch takes its `review.historical-path-absent` guide with it. Second, scoped review measures amendment counts by reading archived predecessor bytes through `readAmendmentInstrument`; the honest replacement is the existing `amendmentCountAudit` not-run absence, which reports the current-only policy reason and a matching absence record without inventing numbers. Third, two location predicates test an absolute-path substring for a `changes/archive` marker; they must use the project-relative bundle phase. The catalog and its test pins are retired together because the guide and the literal lengths encode the removed behavior.
The archive-preservation and bounded-writes instruments are the authority-repaired inline instruments frozen in the predecessor, reparameterized to the new base and own id and reduced to the four permitted paths. They are self-contained POSIX/Bun instruments run through the configured shell (`src/artifact/assertions.ts:719-725`); no helper file or fresh design is introduced, and no adopter-wide Windows guarantee is made.
The reviewed conceptual diagrams below are explanatory. They are explanatory roles of existing functions, not required new classes. Every binding behaviour is repeated in the spec's acceptance criteria.

Alternatives.Alternative: Keep the archived-plan informational notices and the scoped amendment counts. Rejected: both read unrelated or predecessor archive bytes into current review output, which the current-only policy withdraws; the answer is active-plan refusal and honest audit absence, not weaker current checks.

Replace the scoped amendment audit by removing the `amendmentCountAudit` field entirely or by fabricating a zero. Rejected: the field's absence states are part of its honesty contract; a fabricated zero claims a measurement that was never made, and removing the field loses the unscoped `not-run` line. The existing `not-run` status with a reason and absence record is the honest shape.

Introduce a new location helper file or export, or reuse `resolveChangeBundle` to classify archive phase. Rejected as unnecessary: a private expression or function inside the already-scoped `src/review/core.ts` fixes both predicates without a new helper file or export and without a change to `src/grace-cursor.ts`.

Add a second close instrument for the archive or bounded-writes behavior, or attach the review/localization test command to two criteria. Rejected: the evaluator is per criterion and does not deduplicate, so duplicating the command would rerun the whole test pair; one narrow instrument per subject is enough.

Widen this bundle to also carry the gates strict-selected-close work, the planning teaching, the footprint pin, or the README row. Rejected: the predecessor was split precisely because it grew across too many surfaces; the second and third slices own that work and are minted separately.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: The shipped XML parser counts artifact structure; runtime catalog/localization populations and relations are measured through the real exported catalog/localization functions, including `allReviewCodes()`. No post-change total is projected here.
The separate `ngrace status` archive-dependent surface is left to its dependent policy slice; this bundle neither touches nor claims it.

Read-boundary scenario on a fresh unique synthetic project with a cold predecessor cache, carrying one active plan and one archived plan plus a neutral and a misleading parent `changes/archive` root. A call-through spy over the real exported reader records zero archive-plan reads for `runPatternDetectors`, unscoped `runReview`, and selected-active `runReview`, and at least one active-plan read as the positive control. The active absent baseline target and the absent undeclared target each still emit `review.confidently-wrong`; declaring the target and creating the baseline removes them, and exact restoration restores them. The spy and inputs are restored.

Preservation-guard scenario on a disposable post-close-shaped copy at base `61a9e42...`. Guard A (archive): clean baseline exits 0; a tracked byte mutation, the same under `--assume-unchanged` and `--skip-worktree` (while `git diff --quiet` exits 0), an untracked file, an ignored `.DS_Store`, and a file whose name contains the full C-ID each exit 1 and restore to 0; the exact own arrival and an empty nested `run/` directory stay 0. Guard B (bounded writes): clean and the four allowed edits plus own arrival exit 0; an outside-scope tracked edit, that edit under both index flags, an outside-scope tracked addition, and a persistent tracked candidate-lock path each exit 1 and restore to 0. A real `ngrace gate verdict` on the copy records pass clean, refuses with an unchanged ledger when an old archive byte is edited under `--assume-unchanged`, and passes again after exact restoration. Comparisons are bytes and identities only; no archive content is parsed or executed.
